thread:
maya: Quick design review — noticed a couple of weirdnesses in the Rules editor preview when reordering priorities. Dragging rule items sometimes makes the preview list flicker and occasionally duplicates the rule entry. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.fake/snap1.png

jon: Hmm, I can repro. Happens when you drag fast and release near the top edge of the preview. Might be a render/virtualization issue.

sam: Thanks for the report. Can you paste repro steps? I want to try with keyboard reorder too.

maya: Steps: 1) Open a policy with ~8 rules. 2) Drag rule #6 up two positions quickly. 3) Observe preview on the right — flicker + duplicate for ~1s. Only happens when preview is visible and collapsed panels are open.

jon: Repro on Chrome 114. Also saw it on Windows. Not repro on Safari yet.

rachel: Accessibility note: keyboard reorder (move up/down shortcuts) doesn't update the preview's focus announcement. Screen reader only sees the final list but no ARIA alert during the move, so users don't get intermediate feedback. We should add an aria-live region for preview changes.

sam: Agree on aria-live. For the flicker, I'm guessing the preview diff algorithm does an optimistic insert before cleanup. Quick fix: debounce the preview update by 50ms and batch DOM patches. Longer term: sync model updates with the drag state.

jon: UX question: do we want preview to be fully live during mid-drag or should it show a ghost position until drop? If live, we need to make the animation stable. If ghost, we avoid flicker but lose immediate feedback. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

maya: My vote is ghost during drag (show placeholder) — less surprising for users and avoids duplications. We can add micro-copy: "Preview will update on drop" so users know why it's static.

rachel: If ghost, ensure keyboard users get equivalent feedback: announce "item moved to placeholder position" during move. Also update validation messages if reorder triggers rule conflicts.

sam: Implementation plan I propose: 1) During drag: show placeholder in preview, suppress diff patches. 2) On drop: run ordering algorithm, update preview with a 150ms crossfade. 3) If validation errors emerge (e.g., two rules with identical ID or mutually exclusive conditions), show inline banner in preview and tie to rule row with aria-describedby.

jon: Copy tweak for the validation banner: current "Rule conflict" feels vague. How about: "Preview blocked: two rules evaluate identically for some inputs. Open rule X to inspect." Linking to the rule helps.

maya: +1. Also microcopy for empty priority slots: "No rule assigned — requests will fall back to default routing."

rachel: A11y nit: ensure the banner has role="alert" so it is read immediately. And use a visually hidden link text like "Jump to conflicting rule" that screen readers can use.

sam: I pushed a small patch to the sandbox branch that debounces preview updates and adds a placeholder. Deploy-bot: sandbox deploy?

deploy-bot: sandbox deployment started for branch sam/preview-stability at 1881234578. URL: https://sandbox.redwood.fake/preview/1881234578

jon: I checked the sandbox. Dragging now shows placeholder and the flicker gone. Two follow-ups: 1) The crossfade timing feels slow on low-end machines; maybe 120ms instead of 150ms. 2) When you drop and validation banner shows, focus isn't moved to the banner — keyboard users miss it.

sam: I'll shorten the crossfade to 120ms. For focus: on drop, if there are validation issues, programmatically focus the banner and set aria-live to assertive for the message. That should satisfy keyboard+screenreader.

maya: One more UX detail: when reordering multiple selected rules (shift+select), we should show a collapsed stack placeholder in the preview with a count badge, instead of duplicating entries. Handles complex move flows.

jon: Nice. Also can we add a tiny affordance: when you hover the priority handle, show a tooltip "Drag to reorder — keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl+↑↓". Copy should be short.

rachel: A11y test plan suggestion: 1) NVDA/JAWS readthrough of reorder flow, 2) VoiceOver on mac, 3) keyboard-only reordering including multi-select, 4) screen reader announcement timing checks. I can run parts of this.

maya: I'll update the design doc with the ghost behavior and the banner copy. Sam, can you post the sandbox link when ready and note the reduced crossfade?

sam: Will do. Pushing a follow-up in ~30m.

maya: Thanks everyone — this feels a good tradeoff: stable preview, explicit copy, and accessible announcements. We'll capture as a small sprint task and include a unit test for preview state to prevent regressions.

jon: tiny nit for the rules list: keyboard reorder indicator uses blue outline which is same as selection state. Suggest a dashed outline for reorder handle instead so the states are visually distinct.

maya: Noted. rachel, any color contrast concerns with dashed outline?

rachel: Dashed outline is fine as long as focus color meets 3:1 contrast against the background. If not, use a 4:1 color. I'll check values and send a quick PR with tokens.

sam: Sandbox updated: https://sandbox.redwood.fake/preview/1881234590 — crossfade 120ms, placeholder behavior, aria-live window added. Please test and react. :rocket:

maya: Verified. Flicker gone, duplicate not seen. Marking as ready-for-design-review. I'll update the ticket with screenshots and accessibility checklist.

jon: LGTM. Closing thread for now.
